Name: Aircraft Information Extension Format
Description: The ACFT TRE provides miscellaneous information unique to airborne sensors. The ACFT extension is required. A single ACFT extension, containing information relative to the capture of its associated image data will be placed in the respective subheader of every NITF image segment.

AC_MSN_ID.Name: Aircraft Mission Identification
AC_MSN_ID.Description: This is the name of the mission. 'NOT AVAIL' (without quotes) shall be used if a mission name is unavailable.

SCTYPE.Name: Scene Type
SCTYPE.Description: This field represents the scene type, for example, C=Collection Plan, R = Retasked, space = Immediate, or Unplanned.

SCNUM.Name: Scene Number
SCNUM.Description: This value identifies the current scene, and is determined from the mission plan, except for immediate spot scenes, where it has the value 0000.  The scene number is only useful to replay/regenerate a specific scene; there is no relationship between the scene number and an exploitation requirement.

SENSOR_ID.Name: Sensor ID
SENSOR_ID.Description: This value identifies which specific sensor produced the image.

PATCH_TOT.Name: Total Number of Patches
PATCH_TOT.Description: This is the total number of patches contained in this image segment, and therefore, the number of PATCH extensions contained in this image subheader. Not used for EO-IR imagery.

MTI_TOT.Name: Total Number of MTI Packets
MTI_TOT.Description: This value represents the total Number of MTIRP extensions contained in this file. Each MTIRP identifies 1 to 999 moving targets. Shall contain 000 for EO-IR imagery.

PDATE.Name: Processing Date
PDATE.Description: This is the date that the data was processed.  For SAR data, this value represents when the raw complex data was converted to imagery. For EO-IR data, this value represents when image file is created. Where DD represents the day of the month (01 to 31), MMM represents the month (JAN to DEC), and YY represents the two least significant digits of the year. This date changes at midnight UTC.

IMHOSTNO.Name: Immediate Scene Host
IMHOSTNO.Description: This field, together with the immediate scene request ID field, denotes the scene that the immediate was initiated from and can be used to renumber the scene, Example: If the immediate scene was initiated from scene number 123 and this is the third request from that scene, then the scene number field will be zero, the immediate scene host field will contain 123 and the immediate scene request id will contain 00003. When the scene number is greater than 999, this field will only contain the three least significant digits of the scene number; any resulting ambiguity can be resolved by comparing collection times. Shall contain 000 for Pre-Planned scenes.

IMREQID.Name: Immediate Scene Request ID
IMREQID.Description: The standard provides no description for this field.

SCENE_SOURCE.Name: Scene Source
SCENE_SOURCE.Description: This value indicates the origin of the request for the current scene. A scene is single image or a collection of images providing contiguous coverage of an area of interest. 0 = Pre-Planned, 1 to 6 = Sensor Specific: For ASARS-2: 1 = Scene Update (uplink) 2 = Scene Update (manual - via the pilots cockpit display unit) 3 = Immediate Scene (immediate spot or search range adjust) 5 = Preplanned Tape Modification 6 = SSS Other Sensors: TBD.

MPLAN.Name: Mission Plan Mode
MPLAN.Description: This value defines the current sensor specific collection mode.  Where the image extends along an extended path, as with SAR Search mode and EO-IR Wide Area Search modes, the entry and exit locations are the specified latitude, longitude and elevation above mean sea level (MSL) of the planned entry and exit points on the scene centerline of the area to be imaged. Where the image is confined to the area about a single reference point, as with Spot modes and Point Target modes, the entry fields contain the specified reference point latitude/longitude/elevation, and the exit fields are not used. The location may be expressed in either degrees-minutes-seconds or in decimal degrees. The format ddmmss.ssX represents degrees (00 to 89), minutes (00 to 59), seconds (00 to 59), and hundredths of seconds (00 to 99) of latitude, with X = N for north or S for south, and dddmmss.ssY represents degrees (000 to 179), minutes (00 to 59), seconds (00 to 59), and hundredths of seconds (00 to 99) of longitude, with Y = E for east or W for west.

ENTLOC.Name: Entry Location
ENTLOC.Description: The version of the standard used to define this version of the ACFTA TRE provides no description for this field.

ENTELV.Name: Entry Elevation
ENTELV.Description: The version of the standard used to define this version of the ACFTA TRE provides no description for this field.

EXITLOC.Name: Exit Location
EXITLOC.Description: The version of the standard used to define this version of the ACFTA TRE provides no description for this field.

EXITELV.Name: Exit Elevation
EXITELV.Description: The version of the standard used to define this version of the ACFTA TRE provides no description for this field.

TMAP.Name: True Map Angle
TMAP.Description: The true map angle for SAR data in search modes, the true map angle is the angle between the ground projection of the line of sight from the aircraft and the scene centerline. For SAR data in Spot modes, the true map angle is the angle, measured at the central reference point, between the ground projection of the line of sight from the aircraft and a line parallel to the aircraft desired track heading. For EO-IR data, the true map angle is defined in the NED coordinate system with origin at the aircraft (aircraft local NED), as the angle between the scene entry line of sight and the instantaneous aircraft track heading vector. The aircraft trackheading vector is obtained by rotating the north unit vector of the aircraft local NED coordinate system in the aircraft local NE plane through the aircraft trackheading angle. The true map angle is measured in the slanted plane containing the scene entry line of sight and the aircraft track-heading vector. This angle is always positive. A value of 999.999 indicates the true map angle is unavailable.

RCS.Name: RCS Calibration Coefficient
RCS.Description: This field describes the performance calibration value for SAR sensor equipment.

ROW_SPACING.Name: Row Spacing
ROW_SPACING.Description: The row spacing for SAR data represents ground plane distance between corresponding pixels of adjacent rows, measured in feet.  For EO-IR data, this value represents the angle between corresponding pixels of adjacent rows, measured in microradians at center of image.

COL_SPACING.Name: Column Spacing
COL_SPACING.Description: The row spacing for SAR data, this value represents ground plane distance between adjacent pixels within a row, measured in feet. For EO-IR data, this value represents angle between adjacent pixels within a row, measured in microradians at center of image.

SENSERIAL.Name: Sensor Vendor's serial number
SENSERIAL.Description: This is the serial number of the line replaceable unit (LRU) containing EO-IR imaging electronics or SAR Receiver/Exciter involved in creating the imagery contained in this file.

ABSWVER.Name: Airborne Software Version
ABSWVER.Description: This is the airborne software version (vvvv) and revision (rr) numbers.
